Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

I should have protected others and I failed

issues.explanation: The profile only includes Memory and Negative Appraisals, with the formulation showing a strong reciprocal link specifically between these two nodes. The memory items are dominated by trauma-recall qualities and guilt on recall, but 'Body as Enemy' and especially the globally externalized appraisal 'Fear of Harm: You can never know who will harm you' shift toward current somatic threat/general danger beliefs that are not reflected in the memory content and are hard to reconcile with the otherwise memory-centred formulation. Given no active Threat or Trigger links, these appraisal items do not align well with the specified cognitive pattern.

issues.item: Fear of Harm: You can never know who will harm you
issues.explanation: This appraisal is hard to reconcile with the provided cognitive formulation. The only active connections are between Negative Appraisals and Memory, suggesting appraisals should be closely tied to trauma recollection and meaning-making about the event. A generalized interpersonal-danger belief ('You can never know who will harm you') implies an active Threat focus, yet Threat is otherwise unrepresented and all Threat-related edges are inactive. The other appraisal items are self-blaming and memory-linked (weakness, inaction guilt), so this one pulls the profile toward a different formulation not supported elsewhere.

vignette: Carlos Hernandez, a 55-year-old Navy Officer of Latin American descent, had always been proud of his service. But it was during a stint in a war-torn civilian zone that he witnessed an event that would forever alter the way he saw himself and the world around him. As Carlos recounts the day, his voice drops to a whisper, "I remember the smell of smoke, the sound of screams... everything feels so real when I recall it." This sensory overload often leaves him breathless. At times, however, he can only muster a numb recollection, as if the event had happened to someone else. But regardless of how he experiences the memory, one feeling consistently lingers: guilt. In Carlos's mind, his inability to prevent the traumatic event has solidified an unshakeable conviction - that he is weak and failed to protect others when it mattered most. This self-perceived weakness, along with an overwhelming sense of inaction guilt, colors every recollection of the event. "If only I had acted sooner," Carlos tells himself, his eyes clouding over with regret. The memory of that fateful day often intrudes upon his present, triggered by seemingly innocuous stimuli - a particular scent or sound can instantly transport him back to the chaos and destruction he witnessed. And when it does, the cycle begins anew: Carlos's recollection reinforces his negative self-appraisals, which in turn intensify the guilt that accompanies each memory. Carlos's relationship with his partner has suffered as well. His increasing withdrawal and irritability have created tension, leading to arguments about his "distant" behavior. At work, he finds himself questioning every decision, second-guessing whether he truly has what it takes to be a Navy Officer. The weight of these self-doubts is crushing him. Recently, Carlos had an incident during training where he hesitated in responding to a simulated emergency. This momentary lapse sparked a torrent of self-criticism: "What if I fail again? What if others pay the price for my weakness?" For Carlos, this episode was the final straw - it made him realize that his memories and negative appraisals had formed a suffocating cycle he couldn't escape alone. That's when Carlos finally decided to seek help. He hopes therapy will allow him to break free from the grip of guilt and self-doubt, to learn how to manage his memories without letting them define him. But for now, the shadows cast by that traumatic event continue to darken every corner of his life.
